title: Citrix confirms two NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited in attacks
blurb: Two unpatched NetScaler remote code execution flaws are already being exploited in the wild, and Citrix's own advice is to take affected gateways offline rather than wait for a patch.

title: GitHub Actions re-enabled with Mini Shai-Hulud payload still active
blurb: GitHub turned Actions back on for affected repos before the self-propagating supply-chain worm's payload was fully cleared, so infected pipelines can keep spreading it downstream.

title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
blurb: A container isolation bug let one customer's workload see another tenant's data on Cloudflare's platform, underscoring how thin the wall between tenants can be in multi-tenant compute.

title: Minecraft is getting its first new dimension in 14 years, and it's called The Sift
blurb: The Sift is the first entirely new Minecraft dimension since The End, a rare structural addition to a 15-year-old world format rather than another biome pass.

title: After 12 years, Dark Souls 2 is finally playable in co-op without interruptions
blurb: A community mod finally delivers seamless co-op for a 2014 game whose original online design constantly booted party members apart.

title: Black hole jets reach far beyond galaxies' visible edges, potentially deciding their fate
blurb: New observations show supermassive black hole jets extending well past their host galaxy's visible boundary, suggesting they shape galactic evolution more than previously measured.

title: Molecular 'self-destruct' switch discovered: How stressed cells decide between survival and death
blurb: Researchers identified a molecular switch that governs whether a stressed cell repairs itself or triggers programmed death, a mechanism relevant to cancer and degenerative disease.

title: Defeating Satellite Spoofing with Galileo's Encryption
blurb: A breakdown of how Galileo's navigation message authentication cryptographically signs satellite signals so receivers can reject GPS-spoofing attacks.

title: Enormous Fluid Simulation on Flip Dots
blurb: Problem: Surplus flip-dot panels are painful to source and drive, but mitxela wanted a giant interactive "water" display for EMF 2026. Approach: Built custom driver boards for each dot, ran a real-time fluid simulation across the grid, and added a joystick plus an accelerometer so tilting or shaking the cabinet stirs the simulated liquid. Result: A wall of clacking dots that ripples and sloshes convincingly, looks almost 3D from an angle, and reacts physically when nudged. Why it matters: Shows how much custom electronics and software it takes to make old electromechanical hardware feel alive, not just nostalgic. Jargon: Flip-dot display - pixel flipped by a magnet; Fluid simulation - physics model of liquid motion; Accelerometer - motion/tilt sensor.

title: Reverse Engineering Apple's Mikey Chip
blurb: Problem: iPod Classic headsets use an undocumented "Mikey" chip for mic power and buttons; nobody had cracked its protocol in 20 years. Approach: Hemant found one old archived blog post, traced the chip to an I2C bus, found each button is a resistive load causing a voltage drop, then built debug firmware into Rockbox to capture the handshake "chirp." Result: Decoded button detection and the chirp handshake, then submitted the work to Rockbox for official support. Why it matters: Restores wired-headset controls on vintage iPods and shows patient signal analysis can crack silicon with no documentation. Jargon: I2C bus - two-wire chip protocol; Resistive load - button read as resistance; Rockbox - open-source iPod firmware; Chirp - the handshake signal.
